items.title: This Company Will Buy Your AI Training Data
items.summary:
AI companies want your data so badly that we may be entering the era where they just start paying you for it. 👀

I came across a company called Verb that lets you choose what data you’re willing to share, block certain companies, and even set your own price.

And I think this could become a much bigger trend.

As people get more protective of their data—but AI companies need more of it for training and advertising—the solution might simply become: pay people directly.

Obviously, there are some MASSIVE privacy questions here.

So I’m curious: Would you sell your data to big tech if the price was right? 

#AI #Ainews #chatgpt
items.author: Matt Wolfe
items.transcript: AI companies really, really want your data. So much that they're actually now willing to pay you directly for it. So, I recently came across this company called Verb that's actually trying to help you get paid for the data these companies want [music] from you. And no, this is not sponsored by them. I just thought it was an interesting concept. It works by you allowing them to install a tracking script on your phone. Then you decide which data you feel comfortable actually sharing. This could be things like browsing activity, shopping habits, and data export from things like Instagram or TikTok or ChatGPT. And you can turn off specific categories and block companies you don't want having your data and even set your own price for it all. Verb also claims to exclude sensitive info like passwords and text messages and health data. So, I've had this theory that I've talked about a few times in some of my long-form videos where I actually think things like this are more likely to get people paid in the near future than something like a universal basic income. These companies really, really want your data. And people are actually becoming more and more focused on making sure companies can't get your data. So, companies' last resort will just be straight-up paying you for that data so they can train models and better target ads. It could end up being similar to something like UBI, but the companies are paying it out to you instead of the government. Now, is this a good thing? I don't totally know how I feel about this yet. There's some pretty obvious massive privacy trade-offs here, but I do think there are plenty of people out there that are willing to trade privacy for a paycheck. So, I do have a feeling we're going to see a lot of companies trying this in the near future. I'm curious, would you sell your data to Big Tech if the price was right?

items.title: I Built a FREE App That Runs Your Entire Business
items.summary:
I vibe coded a free productivity app that keeps my entire business in one place, and I built it so anyone can download and customize it. I already use an earlier version of this dashboard every day, but this time I rebuilt it from scratch to see how far I could push Codex on a genuinely useful business tool. I used Codex inside ChatGPT for the initial build, then spent hours testing, debugging, and refining it.

The result is Control Center: one dashboard for industry news, brand mentions, reminders, audience analytics, newsletters, and recurring tasks. It connects to Gmail, tracks social growth across YouTube, X, Instagram, and more, and can optionally use OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Grok, or local models to rank and summarize what matters. No AI API key is required. You can install it locally from GitHub for free, customize every section, and optionally host it online.

Download your own control center on GitHub: http://github.com/mreflow/control-center

Discover More:
🛠️ Explore AI T

items.title: How To EASILY Run Local AI Models
items.summary:
You don’t need a massive GPU server to run powerful AI models locally anymore.

Models like Qwen 3.8 27B can run on consumer-grade computers, and LM Studio makes the whole process ridiculously easy.

You just search for the model → choose the highest-quality quantization your computer can handle → download it → start chatting.

LM Studio will even tell you whether a specific version should run on your machine before you download it.

Local models keep getting smaller, more efficient, and more capable. Combined with the extra layer of privacy and data security, it's natural that people are becoming more and more interested in them. 

Are you making the switch to local AI, or are cloud models like ChatGPT and Claude still the best?

#AI #Ainews #aiagents #aitips #chatgpt

items.title: This AI Creates Insane 3D Worlds
items.summary:
This might be one of the coolest AI models I’ve seen all year.

Tencent’s new WorldClaw model can generate an entire editable 3D world from a prompt — not just the environment, but every individual object inside it.

Trees, buildings, carts, lamp posts, terrain, they’re all generated as separate 3D assets you can actually work with.

Under the hood, it combines image generation, segmentation, and Tencent’s Hunyuan 2D-to-3D tech to turn a generated scene into a full collection of 3D objects.

And the use cases could get really interesting.

You could imagine generating game environments in minutes, building virtual worlds for simulations, or even creating environments where robots can train before they ever enter the real world.

Unfortunately we can’t actually play with this model yet, but this is absolutely one I’m keeping an eye on.
